review_items.frank_statement: self.root requires persistent AgencyState/InterestTrace/AutotelicGoal/InitiativePulse plus authority-separated open-web evidence and authenticated direct messages.
review_items.counterhypothesis: The frozen BASE-D V18 surface or G9 primitives cannot represent the new target types without a semantic-language amendment.
review_items.falsifier: A required owner-fixed state/authority relation fails to parse or cannot be represented as records/symbol sums/sets/maps/refs plus typed checker laws without an untyped escape hatch.
independent_checks: Current-run executable V18 parser reconstruction accepted WP03_TYPED_IR_CANDIDATE.clay using existing record/type/Set/Map/Ref primitives.
Current-run mutation checks rejected InitiativePulse amplitude escalation and open-web effect-authority escalation in the candidate typed validator.
adversarial_checks: Range syntax such as Real[0,1] is not required as new surface syntax; bounds can be represented as typed checker laws over Real fields.
Current frontend semantic_hash remains syntax-structural and changes under record-field/set-literal reordering, so parseability alone is insufficient for typed semantic identity.
review_items.reason: The owner-fixed requirements are expressible without reopening the semantic freeze, but WP03 must add a typed canonical IR layer whose semantic identity normalizes explicitly unordered constructs and binds constraints separately from surface parse shape.
review_items.claycode_action: Implement typed IR normalization/checking behind V18; do not change surface grammar unless a later executable counterexample requires it.

review_items.frank_statement: Descriptive capability data must not itself mint effect authority; target effects require deterministic authority separation.
review_items.counterhypothesis: A copyable serialized CapabilityToken record is sufficient as the runtime bearer and no opaque host resource identity is needed.
review_items.falsifier: A target runtime demonstrates authority closure, revocation and anti-forgery using only copyable descriptive data under adversarial forgery/replay tests.
independent_checks: WASI official documentation: applications execute in a capability-based sandbox and start without ambient authority; host grants capabilities explicitly.
WebAssembly Component Model WIT resource documentation: resources are handles to host/component entities, with owned and borrowed handle semantics.
adversarial_checks: Candidate validator explicitly rejects COPYABLE_TEXT as CapabilityToken runtime representation.
review_items.reason: Independent capability/runtime design supports lowering ClayCode capability identity to opaque/owned/borrowed host resources rather than treating descriptive text as bearer authority.
review_items.claycode_action: Keep semantic CapabilityToken record, but require opaque ResourceRef/handle realization at runtime/FFI; exact ownership/borrow semantics remain WP07 lowering design, not a WP01 surface-language amendment.

review_items.frank_statement: ClayCode BASE must represent GWT measurement/intervention receipts and Hyperposition higher-order relation/topology/coupling semantics.
review_items.counterhypothesis: These concepts require new syntax or should remain host-language-only observability metadata.
review_items.falsifier: A required GWT/Hyperposition fixture cannot be represented in typed canonical IR using existing records, refs, sets, enums and explicit epoch/provenance fields.
independent_checks: Current-run candidate parsed HyperRelation and MeasurementReceipt structures under V18 without grammar amendment.
adversarial_checks: Exact final readout schema and higher-order relation reduction semantics were not production-tested in this run.
review_items.reason: Representability is supported at the structural level, but production typed-IR/checker and H1/H2 differential evidence are still absent.
review_items.claycode_action: Include representative HyperRelation/MeasurementReceipt fixtures in WP03 positive/negative corpus and defer promotion until production receipts exist.
